graph.title: Desert Biplane (LEGO 4778-1)

new_part_types.name: Nose base round plate with axle hole (yellow)
Plate 1x4 with two wheel pins (dark red)

notes: The PDF has no inventory pages (only picture steps), so Element IDs are not visible. Catalogue types were chosen by shape and colour is in props. Pieces with no close catalogue match were given descriptive new lego-* type ids.
Several steps (3, 4, 6, 12, 14, 20) show many similar pieces from oblique views; exact piece counts and stud positions are best estimates. Ports used for placement are approximate.
Step 3 sub-assembly: black plate with two stacks of dark red plates and a round plate. Wings rest on the stacks.

The lower wings (steps 10-11) are modelled as a tapered wing plate plus a 2x6 extension each. The upper wing (page 20) is a yellow 2x4 plate, two tapered wings, two extensions, two round plates and a yellow wedge, resting on two dark red struts.
The accessories in step 19 (dark red piece, sextant, binoculars) are placed loosely in the cockpit. Their attachment studs are guessed.
Stickers on the final step are not parts and are omitted.

Pilot legs changed to catalogue type lego-4551179 and torso to lego-4551188 (a matching pair with hip ports), replacing the unreal part numbers. The exact colours (dark grey legs, black jacket with red stripes) are in props only. The pilot sits on the seat via a contact edge.
Goggles port is a hinge kind. The nose round plate is a new type with an axle-hole so it fits the axle. The red base plate, hull pieces and wings have enough distinct ports, so no stud is used twice.

Pilot is built first (page 2) and seated in the cockpit at the end (step 26). The axle end port end.1 is shared by several parts threaded on the same axle (cowling, bush, propeller, nose plate); this is an intentional multi-part join on one axle.

Step 3 sub-assembly: black plate with two stacks of dark red plates and a round plate. Tail wheel, wing mounting and stacks are modelled as stacked on the black plate, with wings resting on the stacks.

The lower wings (steps 10-11) are modelled as a tapered wing plate plus a 2x6 extension each. The upper wing (page 20) is built as a yellow 2x4 plate, two tapered wings, two extensions, two round plates and a yellow wedge, and rests on two dark red struts.
The accessories in step 19 (dark red piece, sextant, binoculars) are placed loosely in the cockpit. Their attachment studs are guessed.
Stickers on the final step (roundels and '4778' on the tail) are not parts and are omitted.
Steps 4 and 5 show a yellow tile/plate at the cockpit end; it is not clearly separable and was not modelled as its own piece.
The shovel in step 18 is clipped to the second side clip plate from step 15.
Pilot (page 2) is built first and seated in the cockpit at the end (step 26).
